lead.hed: Air Force One flew over Neyland Stadium before the Tennessee-Texas game
lead.insight: DVIDS, posted at 4:01 p.m. Eastern: the 134th Air Refueling Wing photographed Air Force One over Neyland Stadium in Knoxville before the University of Tennessee versus University of Texas football game. The caption says the wing supported President Donald Trump's visit to Tennessee. Official still from the flight, not a new policy announcement.
lead.image_credit: Master Sgt. Jonathan Young · DVIDS 9968325 · Public domain · Air Force One over Neyland Stadium, Knoxville, Tennessee, Sept. 26, 2026.

political.hed: NORAD is enforcing weekend flight restrictions over Knoxville and Chicago
political.insight: DVIDS, posted Friday from Tyndall Air Force Base: NORAD will enforce FAA VIP temporary flight restrictions this weekend, Sept. 26–27, over Knoxville, Tennessee, and Chicago. Pilots are told to check notices before each flight. The Knoxville restriction matches today's presidential visit. Enforcement notice, not a new air-defense mission.

political.hed: A new indictment names Mexican state officials in a cartel case
political.insight: Heritage, Friday: the commentary says the administration shifted from targeting cartel workers to a Justice Department indictment that names ten past and present officials of Mexico's ruling party in Sinaloa, including Governor Rubén Rocha Moya. All ten have denied wrongdoing. Commentary on an indictment, not a new statute. Not a ship story.

political.hed: Chinese warships blocked a Philippine resupply run to Second Thomas Shoal
political.insight: USNI News, Friday: Chinese warships and coast-guard cutters blocked a Philippine resupply mission to Second Thomas Shoal on Thursday. Manila's National Task Force said the People's Liberation Army Navy and China Coast Guard tried to hinder the run. The most significant development at that feature in the account. Report of the mission, not a U.S. order.

tech.hed: Treating a child as the opposite sex is not the legal definition of abuse, a report argues
tech.insight: Heritage, Friday: institutions built to protect children are under scrutiny after parents lost custody for refusing to treat a gender-confused child as the opposite sex. The report says those cases rest on an ideological premise, not the legal definition of abuse. Report, not a new statute. Not a ship story.

tech.hed: An essay says a Colombian reactionary also argued for freedom
tech.insight: Law & Liberty, Friday: the essay says the fight between traditionalists and lovers of liberty has missed chances to defend freedom, and points to Nicolás Gómez Dávila, who called himself an authentic reactionary and still argued for it. Essay, not a statute.

culture.hed: An essay ties data centers to the emptying of American churches
culture.insight: American Reformer, Friday: Chris Johnson's essay, Data Centers, Demons, and the De-Churching of America, treats the build-out of data centers as a cultural fact, not only a power-grid story. Argument, not a statute. Not Thursday's marijuana essay.

culture.hed: Beijing is selling a Chinese memoir of Khamenei as a safe friend
culture.insight: Providence, Friday: two months after Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed in U.S.-Israeli strikes in February 2026, Iran's cultural office in Beijing promoted a Chinese memoir of the late supreme leader. The piece reads the afterlife as regime messaging, not a new diplomatic agreement.
